whys: Analysis of how brew method changes caffeine content

comments.author: Kirby64
comments.story: High coffee consumption, brain volume and risk of dementia and stroke
comments.why: Analysis of how brew method changes caffeine content
comments.text: Prep method matters so much though. For comparison, a standard double shot of espresso is typically 18g of coffee. This would yield approximately 110mg of caffeine. By comparison, the same 18g brewed using a pour over method should yield an 8oz cup of coffee with … likely around 170mg of caffeine. comments.author: aphantastic
comments.story: Humans are unreliable models of mouse disease
comments.why: Cited for caffeine content of filter coffee versus espresso
comments.text: 1 cup filter coffee can be 170mg or more. And LD50 isn’t really relevant here, even LD1 levels are deadly to hundreds of millions of people. It’s entirely possible for what some might consider a “normal” amount of coffee to be deadly to many. See other comment for espresso calculations. [VIDEO]

comments.author: FirmwareBurner
comments.story: Espresso Coffee Mitigates the Aggregation of Alzheimer′s Associated Tau Protein
comments.why: Measurement showing filter coffee extracts more caffeine than espresso
comments.text: Not necessarily true, filter extracts more caffeine than espresso at the same soluble extraction levels: [VIDEO] The truth is there is not enough scientific research to compare all brewing methods. Espresso uses high pressure but very short brew times, but filter uses more water and longer brew times therefore the coffee comes out totally different, and that's before we even talk about different grind sizes and roast levels.
